clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old man presented with a 3-month progressive illness characterized by dyspnea on exertion, fatigue, weight loss, and a petechial rash. Initial evaluation was complicated by misattribution to vasculitis/RPGN based on elevated inflammatory markers (elevated CRP, ESR, rheumatoid factor), microscopic hematuria, proteinuria, low C3 complement, and acute kidney injury (creatinine 3.20 mg/dL from baseline 0.89-1.02 mg/dL). However, careful examination revealed a grade III/VI apical systolic murmur radiating to the left axilla, and the patient had pre-existing mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation with leaflet prolapse from prior cardiology evaluation. Transthoracic echocardiogram performed on the day after ED admission demonstrated a vegetation on the posterior mitral leaflet with leaflet thickening, establishing the cardiac source of systemic manifestations. Blood cultures were obtained and IV ceftriaxone was initiated. On hospital day 14, the patient underwent successful bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement with debridement of a 5 mm excrescence on the aortic valve. Histopathology of the excised mitral valve demonstrated fibrosis, extensive acute and chronic inflammation, and necrosis with numerous Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains on Gram's stain, consistent with streptococcal infection. The aortic valve lesion also showed necrosis, inflammation, and Gram-positive cocci. The patient was discharged on hospital day 25 with a plan to complete 4 weeks of intravenous penicillin from the date of surgery, with creatinine improved to 1.2 mg/dL.
